China-Bermuda Agreement on Exchange of Information on Tax Matters (2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bermuda Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 (POCA), as amended; Bermuda Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Code of Practice 2021 (as updated), issued under POCA; Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 (as amended, governing ELP formation and register of partners); Beneficial Ownership (Non-Corporate Entities) Act 2023 and Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2023 (centralized non-public beneficial ownership register); Economic Substance Act 2018 (relevant activity and substance filings).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified constitutional documents and certificate of incorporation/registration of the ultimate holding entity (including parent entity excerpt of members or partners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or notary public in the country of origin of the ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (UK extension covers Bermuda; China-issued documents are apostillable under the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents, effective 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identity document and proof of residential address for each natural-person Ultimate Beneficial Owner and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence, supplemented by regulated-entity verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, where the issuing state is not a party to the Apostille Convention, full consular legalization at the nearest competent consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth / source of funds declaration, including certified bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or regulated financial intermediary maintaining the client relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on notarized signature and bank stamp; notarized English translation where the original is in Chinese or another non-English language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent law enforcement or regulatory authority of the relevant jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; supplementary formalities accepted by the Bermuda Registrar and AML/CFT supervisory authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners above 10%, authorized signatories and beneficial controllers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK OFSI Consolidated Sanctions List, and Bermuda's domestic sanctions instruments. PEP status must be identified under FATF standards; politically exposed persons require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval. The Bermuda supervisory authority requires ongoing transaction monitoring and enhanced scrutiny for PEP-linked ownership structures for the restaurant chain's payment rails and cross-border condiment supply flow.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_ubs_piercing_requirement: The designated AML officer or corporate services provider must identify and verify each individual holding at least 25% economic interest; where ownership is held through a chain of entities, each intermediary company and partnership must be traced until natural persons or a recognized public-listed entity is reached. Nominee interests must be disclosed and the underlying beneficial owner recorded on the private UBO register (Government_Only_Access).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registry General - Registrar of Companies e-Registry (online name request and filing portal via www.registry.gov.bm and government of Bermuda e-services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official business language of Bermuda is English. All proposed entity names must be in Latin alphabet characters. No Chinese-script or other non-Latin script may be used in the registered name; where a Chinese brand name is used commercially, a verified English transliteration must be registered as the sole statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or licensed corporate services provider may file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating grounds of compliance with the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 and distinctiveness compared with existing names. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may (i) apply to the Minister of Finance for ministerial consent to the proposed name, or (ii) resubmit a materially different name with a fresh application fee. Statutory fees for name clearance and reservation must be repaid on each reappraisal; there is no formal hearing unless ministerial review is requested.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or bare mailing address is not permissible as the statutory registered office of a Bermuda Exempted Limited Partnership. The ELP must maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda through a licensed corporate services provider or approved registered-office agent. However, the ELP's actual hotpot restaurant operations, condiment distribution, and merchant acquiring infrastructure will be conducted through foreign operating subsidiaries; Bermuda will retain only the statutory registered office and financial-directorship substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% probability per annum) for a passive, non-resident-owned ELP holding overseas restaurant assets and facilitating pass-through income; likelihood increases to medium (20-40%) if the ELP elects economically substantive activity in Bermuda or is linked to high-volume international payment processing under local merchant acquiring licenses, which may trigger unannounced supervisory visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015 (Bermuda), Parts I to III, sections 1 to 28; Exempted Limited Partnerships (Registration Fees) Regulations 2019; Companies Act 1981 (applicable provisions on charges and corporate administration); Partnership Act 1902 (residual general partnership law)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form ELP-1) filed with the Registrar of Companies for issuance of a Certificate of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Exempted Limited Partnership under Bermuda law; capital contributions are fixed exclusively by the partnership agreement. No escrow or capital deposit account is required. Registration fees and annual government fees are payable from general partnership funds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The General Partner, by unanimous written resolution, resolves as follows. FIRST: the Partnership Agreement of the Exempted Limited Partnership is approved and adopted in final form. SECOND: the General Partner is authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Registrar of Companies, Bermuda. THIRD: the registered office is established at the premises of the appointed resident representative, who is authorized to accept service of process. FOURTH: the principal business scope is confirmed as overseas directly-operated hotpot dining and condiment supply with all lawful ancillary activities. FIFTH: authorized signatories and officers are appointed with signing authority for bank, licensing and administrative matters. SIXTH: all incidental documents necessary to give full effect to these resolutions are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the Exempted Limited Partnership Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (online corporate registry portal via gov.bm)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation application for the proposed ELP name, ensuring it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, partnership, or other exempted entity. Specify the intended overseas restaurant and condiment supply business to enable the Registrar’s screening of prohibited or misleading terms. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee and obtain the reservation certificate, which is valid for a defined reservation period.
required_dossiers: Copy of payment receipt for name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity or prohibited wording, the applicant may submit up to three alternative names, request written reasons, and seek reconsideration by the Registrar under section 6 of the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified Bermuda legal counsel and a notary public admitted in Bermuda or a recognized British Overseas Territory
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Partnership Agreement setting out capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, admission and withdrawal of partners, delegated management authority of the General Partner, indemnification, and dissolution mechanics. Confirm the General Partner may be a non-resident entity while the ELP must maintain a resident representative. Attest the signatures of all partners before a notary public, and for corporate partners attach certified certificate of incumbency and board consents.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incumbency for each corporate partner
Certified constitutional documents of corporate partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requires amendments to internal governance provisions, the partners may execute a supplemental deed of amendment and file a Notice of Amendment with the Registrar for recordal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership and Registration Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and lodge Form ELP-1 together with the prescribed registration fee. The Declaration must state the ELP name, registered office address in Bermuda, nature of business (overseas direct-operated hotpot dining and condiment supply), term (if any), the name and address of the General Partner, and confirmation that no public solicitation of partnership interests has occurred. Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Notarized extract of the Partnership Agreement
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the applicant must respond in writing within 14 days with clarifications or amended Declaration pages. A refusal may be appealed by originating summons to the Supreme Court of Bermuda or challenged by judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Resident Representative and Establishment of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (through a licensed corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Bermuda-licensed corporate services provider to act as resident representative and to make available a physical registered office in Bermuda at which legal process and official notices may be served. Confirm the registered office address and file the Notice of Registered Office (Form ELP-4) within the statutory period. The resident representative must satisfy the Registrar’s fit-and-proper assessment.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed service provider
Identity and verification documents of the representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident representative is deemed unfit or disqualified, the ELP must appoint a replacement within 21 days and file a fresh consent and Notice of Registered Office with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Tax Exemption Certificate and Completing Beneficial Ownership Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies; Office of the Tax Commissioner, Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the ELP tax exemption certificate confirming exemption from all Bermuda income, profits, and capital gains taxes until a specified exempt date. Verify that the overseas restaurant operation does not constitute a Bermuda economic substance relevant activity, and file any required economic substance declaration if the partnership has Bermuda administrative presence. Submit the Beneficial Ownership Register details to the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption or economic substance declaration is queried, submit a written explanation evidencing the overseas business premises, employees, and operational management outside Bermuda, and file an amended declaration within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Business License Application and Host-Market Licensing Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Business Licensing Authority, Department of Business Development; host-country food safety authority for the overseas restaurant premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Bermuda Business License application for the ELP’s administrative presence, if any deemed trade is conducted in Bermuda. Prepare and coordinate the host-jurisdiction restaurant operating license, food establishment health permit, liquor license (where applicable), and condiment food manufacturing or repacking permit. Ensure the corporate records, signing authorities, and partnership certificates are available for the overseas licensing bodies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership and tax exemption certificate
Partnership Agreement excerpt evidencing authorized signatories
Host-country restaurant license and health permit applications
Food safety management plan and hazard analysis critical control point (HACCP) documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Bermuda Business Licensing Authority imposes conditions or refuses the license, the ELP may appeal to the Business Licensing Appeal Board within 21 days and submit supplementary corporate and financial evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bermuda Business Licensing Authority (Department of Business Development, Ministry of Finance); Department of Health Environmental Health Branch for food establishment permits; host-country municipal or national food service authority for the overseas directly-operated restaurant
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Restaurant Business License (Class A – Full-Service Dining) and Food Establishment Health Permit; host-country Food Service Establishment License and Condiment Manufacturing/Repacking Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Government of Bermuda; host-country environmental protection agency for the overseas operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration and Screening (Not a Scheduled Project) — no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report required for a single hotpot restaurant unit below the Schedule thresholds; mandatory screening for commercial kitchen discharge, grease waste, ventilation, and cooking fume emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater shall meet municipal sewer discharge thresholds (pH 6.0 to 10.0; oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L); grease traps of adequate capacity must be installed, serviced, and logged; cooking fume extraction systems must achieve particulate filtration efficiency of at least 95% with odor control; kitchen exhaust VOC and volatile oil mist limits must comply with published air emission thresholds; edible oil waste and grease trap sludge must be removed by a licensed waste carrier and disposed of under commercial and hazardous waste rules; no untreated effluent may be discharged to public drains or groundwater.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service or host fire authority; structural load inspection and occupancy load assessment for dining hall and kitchen; automatic fire suppression and commercial kitchen hood suppression system inspection; emergency exits, lighting, and fire alarm certification; workplace safety clearance for commercial kitchen equipment, gas cylinder storage, and hotpot fuel systems; annual gas safety, electrical installation, and ventilation maintenance certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (administering the Payroll Tax Act 1995, the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 and the Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax); the Registry of Companies (entity formation, registration number, annual returns and economic substance declarations); the Business Licensing Authority (trade licence issuance); and the Bermuda Customs Department, Ministry of Finance (import/export tariffs and ASYCUDA World clearance). Principal e-portals: taxcommissioner.gov.bm for e-filing, the government e-services single window for business licensing, and the ASYCUDA World customs portal. For any UK trading establishment, HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) is the separate competent authority; there is no joint UK/Bermuda tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Bermuda imposes no income tax, corporation tax or capital gains tax, and issues no general-purpose income-tax TIN. For a foreign-owned Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP), the procurement sequence is: (1) appoint a licensed Bermuda corporate services provider/resident agent; (2) file the Declaration of Limited Partnership and partnership agreement with the Registrar of Companies under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015 and obtain the Certificate of Registration; the entity registration number functions as the primary statutory identifier/TIN and must be quoted on all filings, invoices and banking documentation; (3) apply for a Business Licence in the restaurant/food-service category from the Business Licensing Authority, with annual fees assessed on published gross-receipts bands; (4) if the ELP engages Bermuda-resident employees, register as an employer with the Tax Commissioner for Payroll Tax and with the Bermuda Social Insurance Board; a foreign ELP with no Bermuda employees requires no payroll TIN; (5) register with Bermuda Customs as an importer/exporter in ASYCUDA World for any movement of goods, including condiment consignments; (6) if the group is within the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million), register for CIT and file the annual economic substance declaration; otherwise, only the annual ELP return and economic substance declaration are due.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope; Tax_Exempt_Zone (the ELP holds 'exempted' status under Bermuda law, is fiscally transparent for Bermuda purposes, and Bermuda taxes only Bermuda-source items such as payroll, imports and in-scope multinational CIT; the ELP registers as a non-resident partnership, and foreign-source and offshore trading income are outside the Bermuda tax net)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) US check-the-box election under IRC section 7701 and Treas. Reg. section 301.7701-2/3 (Form 8832): a multi-member foreign ELP defaults to partnership classification and a single-member ELP defaults to disregarded-entity status; an affirmative election to be taxed as a corporation is available where US tax planning requires it; (2) Hybrid mismatch disciplines: the ELP can be positioned as a hybrid or reverse-hybrid for UK/US purposes, but the UK hybrid mismatch rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6A) and OECD Action 2 rules must be monitored to prevent denied deductions or double non-taxation; (3) Economic Substance (Bermuda) Act 2018: the ELP must annually select, in the declaration filed with the Registrar, whether it is a pure equity holding entity or is carrying on one of the defined relevant activities, and must meet the corresponding substance requirements; (4) Corporate Income Tax Act 2023: in-scope multinational groups may elect to apply the Bermuda QDMTT safe harbour and obtain credit/coupon treatment for qualifying domestic top-up tax, consistent with OECD Pillar Two.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/sales tax in Bermuda; the jurisdiction's indirect revenue instruments are customs import tariffs under the Customs Tariff Act 1973, plus a Hotel Occupancy Tax limited to accommodation (not applicable to restaurant turnover). A hotpot restaurant generating dine-in, take-away and condiment sales in overseas markets is instead exposed to the host jurisdiction's indirect tax (e.g., UK VAT at standard 20% on restaurant supplies), which arises outside Bermuda's fiscal jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable (BMD): Bermuda levies no VAT/GST and therefore prescribes no turnover-based indirect-tax registration threshold. All commercial importers must register with Bermuda Customs and lodge declarations in ASYCUDA World from the first import; a Business Licence (restaurant/food-service category) is a condition precedent to trading; payroll tax registration is triggered by the first Bermuda-resident employee with no de minimis wage threshold; CIT registration applies only where the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least EUR 750 million.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Bermuda has no real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no e-invoicing API clearance and no digital stamp requirement. Mandatory electronic filing applies to: customs declarations via ASYCUDA World (UN/EDIFACT or web declarations); payroll tax and CIT returns via the Tax Commissioner's e-filing portal; and business licence applications/renewals via the Bermuda online licensing service. Invoices must still comply with general record-keeping and business-licence rules, and source records must be retained for the applicable statutory audit windows for post-clearance and tax audits. For the UK operating entity, HMRC Making Tax Digital-compatible records and the future UK e-invoicing mandate roadmap will apply separately.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Bermuda has no VAT, so no domestic 'zero-rating' claim mechanism exists. Exports of tangible goods from Bermuda, including proprietary hotpot sauces, condiments and food ingredients consigned to the chain's overseas restaurants, are outside the scope of Bermuda customs duty and are exported free of any Bermuda export duty. Eligibility conditions: (1) the goods must physically leave Bermuda and be reported on an electronic export declaration in ASYCUDA World naming the ELP as exporter; (2) the ELP must hold a valid Business Licence and be registered with Customs as an exporter; (3) the commercial invoice, packing list and transport document must evidence the international movement; (4) where duty-paid goods are imported into Bermuda and subsequently re-exported, a customs drawback claim under the Customs Act 1968 requires proof of export within the statutory period and confirmation that no local consumption occurred; (5) services supplied by the ELP to non-residents (franchise, management, offshore catering and logistics services) are not within the charge to any Bermuda indirect tax; import VAT/GST, if any, is collected by the destination jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic filing)
Commercial Invoice (quoting the ELP registration number and Business Licence number)
Packing List (item-level HS commodity codes, weights and values)
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Certificate of Origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed at destination)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing proceeds repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Bermuda Customs may conduct post-clearance audits to verify export and drawback claims; over-declarations or drawback claims based on false documentation are clawed back with interest. Fraudulent or negligent export documentation attracts penalties under the Customs Act 1968, including forfeiture of goods, monetary penalties up to three times the duty evaded, and imprisonment upon indictment, with vessels/aircraft implicated also exposed to seizure. False returns to the Tax Commissioner under the Payroll Tax Act 1995, Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 and Business Licensing Act 1996 are subject to surcharges, fines, daily default penalties and director/partner liability, and fraudulent evasion constitutes a predicate money-laundering offence under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 enabling confiscation of assets. Although Bermuda statute imposes no exchange-control requirement, the 180-day export-proceeds repatriation covenant is maintained as group treasury and transfer-pricing discipline to support the documentary chain for customs drawback, to substantiate economic substance, and to reduce the risk that the ELP is found to be carrying on a UK trade through the actions of a UK permanent establishment or a UK-dependent agent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) — the de facto central bank and the sole exchange-control administrator of Bermuda, a British Overseas Territory. The BMA is constituted under the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 and exercises its statutory powers through the Exchange Control Act 1972, the Exchange Control Regulations 1972, the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1999, and the AML/ATF framework aligned with the Financial Action Task Force; the Bank of England retains no direct licensing function over Bermuda deposit takers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Bermuda maintains a fully convertible current account and an open capital account for non-resident-controlled exempted limited partnerships. The Bermudian dollar is pegged at 1:1 to the United States dollar and licensed banks freely convert BMD into USD, GBP, EUR, and other major currencies for trade, investment, and operating purposes. There are no exchange-control permits, prior consents, or profitability tests applicable to inbound subscriptions, capital distributions, or partnership profit allocations of a non-resident ELP, and because Bermuda levies no income tax, corporation tax, capital-gains tax, or withholding tax, the profit-remittance hurdle is limited to documentary proof rather than tax clearance: capital-account statements, the register of limited partners, and an economic-substance filing position must support each distribution. The only practical convertibility friction arises from the requirement that every flow traverse a licensed bank's AML/ATF, sanctions-screening, and travel-rule compliance framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Bermuda imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime: there is no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no requirement to convert foreign-currency export earnings into BMD. Export receipts derived from the overseas hotpot dining and condiment-supply business (royalties, management fees, goods sales) may be retained in USD, GBP, or EUR in free foreign-currency accounts or converted as treasury policy dictates; the BMA only requires the licensed bank to record the receipt in the customer's account and to report aggregated balance-of-payments statistics in standard regulatory returns.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Treasury Account (USD/BMD/GBP multi-currency)
Capital Subscription Escrow Account and Operational Account with SWIFT/Correspondent Banking (USD/GBP/EUR)
Operational Account for domestic clearing and merchant-settlement sweeps
Commercial Operational and Trade Finance Account for documentary credits and condiment-supply export settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: High for the UK operating layer via a GB FCA-regulated EMI or electronic-money account, but Low-to-Medium for the Bermuda ELP as the direct account holder of a pure offshore digital EMI. Legal Constraints: EMIs cannot provide deposit-taking, documentary-credit, or lending facilities; most EMIs reject Bermudian pass-through vehicles where the general partner is a licensed corporate-services provider and the economic activity sits in the UK or Asia; the Bermuda Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Rules 2018 and the UK FCA Payment Services Regulations require full originator/beneficiary travel-rule data for every qualifying cross-border transfer. The recommended architecture is a dual rail: a tier-1 Bermuda bank account as the statutory treasury anchor, plus a GB FCA-authorised EMI account for European merchant-acquiring settlement, supplier disbursements, and fast GBP clearing, with contractual segregation of client funds and no deposit-taking exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Bermuda licensed banks operate a hybrid physical-presence rule: the general partner (a Bermuda-licensed corporate-services provider) and at least one natural-person authorized signatory must attend an in-person or live-video KYC interview, and remote onboarding is permitted only where identity documents are certified by a Bermuda attorney-at-law or an in-country bank relationship manager. Individual limited partners may complete remote onboarding using apostilled passports, source-of-wealth evidence, and banker's references, but the general partner remains the primary point of accountability. Overseas UK subsidiary directors must separately execute notarized board resolutions and complete the bank's cross-border corporate mandate, with the UK company registration number and registered-office details included in the KYC pack.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk UBO nexus and source-of-funds opacity: the hotpot restaurant chain's founder and Chinese resident investors seek to fund a Bermuda ELP from mainland China or Hong Kong, and the bank flags the absence of verifiable personal wealth and the PRC capital-control context.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BMA standard beneficial-ownership declaration certified by the Bermuda registered agent; notarized passports and residential-address verification; 24-month personal bank statements and tax records evidencing lawful wealth accumulation; PRC SAFE outbound-ODI approval or Hong Kong outbound-investment filing evidencing lawful cross-border capital movement; PEP/sanction-clearance report where applicable; a written source-of-funds memorandum tracing the contribution from the remitting bank account to the ELP subscription escrow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore pass-through vehicle mismatch: a tax-transparent exempted limited partnership with no Bermuda payroll, no premises, and no management substance, while all restaurant operations are conducted in the UK and other overseas markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda certificate of exemption and ELP registration issued under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992; executed partnership agreement and register of limited partners; registered-agent and registered-office confirmation; a non-resident-for-exchange-control declaration or an Economic Substance Act filing position; audited or reviewed financial statements; annual compliance certificates; group organizational chart and service agreements demonstrating the ELP as the brand-holding, IP-holding, and treasury conduit for the overseas hotpot dining and condiment-supply business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive F&B revenue profile: the bank perceives elevated money-laundering risk from daily merchant-acquirer settlement, POS terminal cash mixing, and commingling of restaurant revenue across multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-acquiring agreements with verifiable UK/European acquirers and terminal proofs; EPOS/Z-reports, daily MIS revenue reports, and acquirer settlement statements; VAT and corporation-tax filings of the UK operating entity; supplier invoices, stock records, bills of lading, and condiment-sale contracts; a formal cash-handling policy and cash-transfer schedule; a board-approved account-usage matrix segregating merchant settlement, payroll, supplier payables, and royalty remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment and cross-border disbursement anomalies: the bank flags long payment chains from Bermuda to UK/Asia suppliers through EMIs or third-party intermediaries, and mismatches between declared payment purpose and underlying trade documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: All underlying contracts (real-estate leases, franchise agreements, procurement orders, intercompany service agreements) with invoice-to-payment reconciliation; annotated payment-flow diagrams linking each transaction to commercial duty; UK restaurant licences such as food-premises registration and alcohol licence; landlord and utility contracts evidencing an active operating footprint; board minutes authorizing account opening, authorized signatories, and payment-frequency schedules; CMR or bill-of-lading evidence for condiment exports; and a compliance covenant that no funds will be commingled with unrelated third-party traffic.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202/COV for bank-to-bank reallocation) into the Bermuda Capital Escrow Account, with USD cleared via Fedwire/CHIPS and GBP cleared via CHAPS through the bank's London correspondents. Every remittance must carry a precise purpose code — for example INVEST — contribution to exempted limited partnership — and reference the ELP registration number, the subscriber name, and the drawdown schedule; the receiving bank matches the source account against the certified register of limited partners and the source-of-funds dossier before releasing escrowed funds to the Operational Account. Where the contributing investor is a PRC or Hong Kong entity, the originating bank must evidence SAFE outbound-ODI registration or the applicable Hong Kong outbound-investment filing, and the Bermuda bank must complete the BMA travel-rule and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) verification, including full originator and beneficiary name, address, and account number. No case-by-case BMA exchange-control consent is required for a non-resident ELP, but each escrow release must be supported by a GP-signed capital-drawdown notice and posted to the partnership capital-account ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed over four clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 credits for open-account supplier payments in USD, GBP, or EUR, each carrying the relevant purpose code and backed by invoices or proforma contracts; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) and standby credits (MT760) arranged through the Bermuda bank's London or New York correspondent network for bulk condiment and equipment imports, with presentation of bills of lading, packing lists, certificates of origin, and food-safety certificates; (iii) MT202/COV interbank transfers for treasury concentration and rebalancing between the Bermuda anchor account, the UK operating accounts, and the EMI corridor; and (iv) local merchant-acquiring/POS rails for daily restaurant card settlements, with sweeps from the UK acquirer to the EMI and onward to the Bermuda treasury account on a T+1/T+2 basis. For RMB-denominated supply payables, settlement is executed through the Hong Kong offshore-CNH clearing network (Bank of China (Hong Kong)) and converted into USD or GBP via a licensed FX counterparty; every payment must be paired with underlying trade documents to pass the bank's AML reference-matching and source-of-funds review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards in USD/GBP, USD/EUR, and USD/CNH executed with licensed Bermudian or UK banks, supported by a genuine commercial underlying such as trade invoices, royalty flows, or payroll calendars.

Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (USD/CNH NDFs) used to hedge Chinese condiment-supply payables where RMB is not physically deliverable offshore, with written treasury policy and underlying exposure documentation.
Cross-currency swaps in USD/GBP and USD/CNH to match the maturity profile of capital injections and trade-disbursement flows, executed under an ISDA or bank master agreement.

Plain-vanilla FX options and collars, permitted only where the bank's derivatives licence covers the ELP and where the instruments are documented as bona-fide commercial hedges rather than speculative treasury trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Limited Partnership Annual Declaration (Form ELP/AD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Companies and Partnerships Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of BMD 500 plus BMD 30 per day (max BMD 2,000); continued default may result in the Registrar serving a strike-off notice with 60-day cure period, leading to automatic dissolution of the ELP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance (ESR) Annual Filing and Notice (if in scope)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Economic Substance Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial reporting period (mandatory for entities claiming non-Bermuda tax resident status or carrying out relevant activities; otherwise an annual nil declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of BMD 100 per day (max BMD 10,000) for non-filing; severe or persistent non-compliance can trigger a default assessment notice, financial penalties up to BMD 200,000, and potential termination of the ELP's tax resident status or prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exempted Limited Partnerships are not audited by default; a compulsory audit arises only if required by the Partnership Agreement, creditor mandates, or if the ELP exceeds BMD 10 million annual turnover and is carrying on a 'relevant activity' in Bermuda under the Economic Substance Act. For an overseas restaurant chain, if the ELP is purely a non-resident holding entity, no Bermudian audit is triggered; the operating subsidiary abroad is audited in its local jurisdiction.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for any consolidated group financial statements prepared voluntarily or for the benefit of limited partners); Local GAAP (Bermuda) otherwise accepted; for the HK/foreign operating entity, applicable local accounting standards (e.g., HKFRS/IFRS) govern.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015 and the Bermuda AML/ATF frameworks, the ELP must maintain a register of beneficial owners showing individuals who hold more than 25% interest or control. This register is not filed publicly but the Registered Representative must confirm its accuracy annually in the ELP's Annual Declaration. Any change in limited partner interests or distribution of shares requires an updated declaration and, if the ultimate owner citizenship changes, a new UBO registry entry. Failure to update UBO data for 30 days exposes the ELP and each general partner to a BMD 5,000 fine.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500 – 3,000 per annum (includes local registered agent, registered office, and filing service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 – 8,000 per annum (only if required by the Partnership Agreement or an audit is demanded by an overseas parent, commercial lender, or Bermuda ESR obligations; typically waived for a dormant holding ELP)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15.0% under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (CITA), chargeable solely on in-scope constituent entities of MNE groups with consolidated global revenue of €750 million or more; out-of-scope entities such as a standalone hotpot restaurant chain suffer a 0% Bermuda entity-level income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for the target ELP below the GloBE €750m scoping threshold. In-scope groups may claim the GloBE Substance-Based Income Exclusion (SBIE, 5% of eligible payroll and tangible asset costs during the transition), Qualified Refundable Tax Credits, and use the ELP's pass-through classification to avoid entity-level taxation; partner-level taxation only.
